jobs.occupation: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description:
**Our Tech Stack: https://stackshare.io/companies/sedna

**About Sedna:

**Sedna is at the forefront of revolutionising the operating system for shipping. Our AI-powered platform is designed to make global trade more efficient, transparent, and sustainable. As we continue to grow and innovate, we are looking for exceptional talent to join our journey and contribute to our mission of transforming the shipping industry .

You can find out more about us on our website: https://sedna.com/

**About the role

**This role focuses on contributing to the design, development, and evolution of Sedna’s VMS (Voyage Management System). It's a mature, highly specialised platform that shipowners, operators and charterers use to run chartering, voyage operations, cargo and freight/hire invoicing.

VMS has a Java backend exposing a REST API used by our own web client (React) and directly by customers' integrations. Data lives in Oracle, including a significant amount of business logic in PL/SQL. It runs on AWS and builds through GitLab CI/CD.

Sedna VMS is in use 24/7 by shipping companies worldwide. Customers run their daily operations and invoicing on it, so correctness, performance and reliability directly affect their business.

You will play a key part in raising standards and delivering new features. You'll take real ownership of features and of how they behave in production, on a product customers run their business on, and help shape how the platform evolves. You'll work with modern AI-assisted development tools as part of everyday engineering.

**How you’ll make an impact

****Engineering and feature development

**This role contributes to both backend and frontend development. Day-to-day responsibilities include understanding requirements, shaping technical approaches, writing code, and contributing to automated tests. Development work spans a mix of new features, improvements, and maintenance, driven by both customer and product needs.

**System architecture and modernisation

**The role includes participating in ongoing efforts to refine and modernise the platform. This involves contributing to technical upgrade work, improving system structure, and supporting longer-term architectural direction as the product grows. Opportunities exist to participate in design discussions and help shape solutions that improve system performance, reliability, and extensibility.

**Quality, testing, and delivery practices

**The team maintains a focus on software quality. We combine unit tests, API regression tests (Postman) and UI tests (Playwright) with peer code review on every merge request. Releases are built and tested through GitLab CI/CD. We're actively improving here: getting more of our test suites running automatically in CI and making them reliable. Engineers who want to drive that, will have room to do it.

**Collaboration with product and customer-facing teams

**The role involves close collaboration with product managers through refinement, planning, and solution discussions. Engineers also interact with Customer Support on cases that need engineering input, and, for larger projects, join customer conversations to validate technical approaches.

**Continuous improvement and documentation

**We treat documentation, including API references, design decisions and runbooks, as part of delivering a change. Much of VMS's knowledge still sits with experienced team members, and capturing it in written, searchable form is an active priority. We also reserve time for technical debt and internal improvements.

**In your first 90 days, you can expect

**

• Month 1: Build your understanding of Sedna’s architecture and our products. Get set up with the VMS codebase, your dev environment and the release process, and ship your first changes. Meet your team, product manager and key customer-facing colleagues. Learn the maritime workflows our customers depend on.

• Month 2: Take ownership of a well-scoped piece of work from refinement with product through to release. Contribute to design discussions, give timely and constructive code review feedback. Shadow the on-call rotation and get familiar with runbooks and production tooling.

• Month 3: Lead the technical approach on a complex feature or improvement within your team, working independently and raising risks and dependencies early. Join the on-call rotation. Contribute improvements to tests, runbooks or documentation based on what you found hard to learn, and support technical validation in a customer conversation where relevant.

**What we're looking for:

****Essential experience

**Candidates typically bring three+ years of professional engineering experience from a comparable environment. Experience working on production systems where quality and reliability are important. Familiarity with a JVM language (Java, Kotlin, Scala) or a similar backend language, React or another modern frontend framework. Strong SQL and relational database skills, ideally Oracle or PostgreSQL, including query performance. Experience supporting production systems: diagnosing incidents from logs and metrics. Prior on-call experience is a plus.

**Critical skills

**A strong grasp of building and maintaining features within a larger system is helpful. Confidence with automated testing, CI/CD pipelines, and code review workflows is expected. Clear thinking, good problem-solving ability, and the capacity to work with domain-heavy logic contribute to success in the role. Experience with enterprise or workflow-driven applications is an advantage.

**Traits and mindset

**Curiosity and a willingness to learn the maritime domain are appreciated. A collaborative working style, comfort sharing ideas in cross-functional settings, and the ability to work independently when needed all support strong performance. Adaptability is important as the product and architecture continue to evolve.

**Core competencies

**Systems thinking, ownership of outcomes, strong communication skills, and effective collaboration are central to this role. A motivation to create value for customers and contribute to a stable, evolving platform is essential.

**What’s In Store for You

**

• A strong team. You’ll join a global team of senior and staff engineers who set a high bar and will help level you up.

• A generous salary and benefits package (depending on experience) + private medical, equity, health and wellbeing benefits, home internet contribution

• Scalability challenges. You’ll be a part of evolving our VMS system as we further develop in to a product led company.

• Customer impact. Real customers use our products everyday, you'll see your work impacting real people.

• Collaboration & autonomy. Plenty of heads-down technical work, but also close partnership with product engineers and engineering leadership.

**Our Values:

**Finally, culture is important to us, so we also look for candidates who share our values:

**Stay Ahead, Stay Agile

**

• We don’t just adapt-we anticipate change and act with confidence.

• Curiosity, data, and customer insights help us stay ahead of the curve.

• We embrace challenges as opportunities and remain resilient under pressure.

• By staying open to new ideas and ways of working, we lead the future.

**Execute With Focus

**

• We turn strategy into action, delivering measurable results that matter.

• Every initiative counts-discipline and ownership drive business impact.

• We make smart decisions with speed, balancing pace and precision.

• Clear priorities keep us focused on what moves the needle.

**Work Together, Win Together

**

• Collaboration is our superpower-we succeed as one team, internally and with customers.

• We co-create solutions, seek feedback, and build the future of Sedna together.

• Strong relationships are built on trust, respect, and shared goals.

• By aligning across teams and with customers, we unlock greater impact.

jobs.occupation: Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Do you have experience developing medical devices? Would you like to be part of developing innovative products that make a meaningful difference to patients, while applying your skills in a global MedTech company that is helping shape the future of endoscopy?

Then your next career move could be as a Systems Engineer with Ambu.

**Be a Key Player in Engineering & Imaging

**In this exciting role, you will be a key contributor within our R&D organization and a leading technical member of a product development project. You will play a central role in shaping and delivering innovative endoscopy solutions, directly contributing to Ambu’s future success and to improved outcomes for patients and healthcare professionals.

As part of this position, you will join a team responsible for developing a go-to-market solution that introduces new product features AI capabilities to our existing portfolio of display units. This will enable us to gain valuable experience with AI-enabled solutions while preparing for the development of our next-generation display unit. The solution will support our current portfolio of endoscopy products while also laying the foundation for future platforms, capabilities, and product offerings.

You will be part of our Global Systems Engineering department and report to the Systems Engineering Team Manager. The position is based at our headquarter in Ballerup, Denmark, where you will join a collaborative, professional, and globally connected team.

We foster a strong culture of innovation, with a clear focus on fast time-to-market while remaining deeply committed to developing the right products to meet customer and user needs, ultimately improving patient care. This requires the ability to navigate complex medical device development and bring different technologies, disciplines, and perspectives together into coherent product solutions.

You will join a truly global Systems Engineering team of 22 highly skilled and motivated colleagues based across different locations. The team is part of Engineering & Imaging within our R&D organization and brings together a diverse mix of backgrounds, perspectives, and expertise. What really stands out is the team’s strong collaborative spirit and proven track record of successfully bringing Ambu’s innovative products to market, making it a great environment in which to learn, grow, and contribute.

**Global, User-Driven Innovation: From Idea to Launch

**As a Systems Engineer, you will hold the overall technical view of the product and help subject matter experts, project team members, and other stakeholders understand each other and work effectively together.

You will be leading technical alignment and discussions in the project team to find the right solution , helping drive and maintain the overall technical solution and ensuring coherence across the different technologies and disciplines involved. You will navigate technical trade-offs, facilitate decisions, and ensure that the product solution remains aligned with user needs, business objectives, regulatory requirements, and the overall system architecture.

You will create, facilitate, and review key product development documentation, including requirements, design inputs, design outputs, and technical reviews. You enjoy working in cross-functional project teams, finding pragmatic solutions to complex technical challenges, and ensuring an appropriate level of documentation and technical rigor.

You will be involved throughout the product development lifecycle, from early scope investigation and concept development through design, integration, verification and validation, and ultimately market launch.

We work in a hybrid setup, typically with minimum three days on-site in Ballerup, providing flexibility while maintaining strong team connections.

**Your Responsibilities

**

• Define, plan, document, and technically manage product development activities within the project to ensure the product is delivered in accordance with the defined design objectives and development plan.

• Identify and understand stakeholder and user needs through engagement with key stakeholders and users.

• Analyze and decompose user needs, business needs, and system requirements into clear and actionable product and development requirements.

• Leading technical alignment and discussions with the Project Manager and relevant Line Managers.

• Ensure alignment with product and technology architectures and promote the appropriate reuse of existing design solutions across the R&D organization.

• Investigate and scope new product concepts and solutions within existing or new clinical areas, building on Ambu’s technologies and capabilities.

• Establish and maintain the overall technical overview of the product, including system interfaces, dependencies, and trade-offs between technologies and design solutions.

• Ensure development, documentation, verification, and testing activities are performed in accordance with applicable FDA, ISO, IEC, and internal quality requirements.

Your stakeholder base will be broad, and you will collaborate across Ambu’s global organization, with functions involved throughout product development, as well as externally with users, knowledge centers, technical partners, and suppliers.

Our production sites are located in Malaysia, China, the USA, and Mexico, and we collaborate with KOLs and development centers across Europe, Asia, and the US. Some travel should therefore be expected, approximately 20 days per year.

**Suggested Candidate Profile

**Setting you up for success is one of our cornerstones. We imagine that you are proactive, driven, committed, and comfortable taking responsibility and ownership. You are thorough and quality-minded, with strong interpersonal skills and good situational awareness, enabling you to work effectively in cross-functional and global teams.

**Skills

**Skills and experience can be gained in many different ways, and we understand that the best fit for a role cannot always be defined on paper. That said, you are likely to thrive in this role if you bring:

• A degree or professional background in electrical engineering, mechatronics, mechanical engineering, biomedical engineering, or a similar technical field, together with relevant hands-on product development experience.

• Experience developing medical devices, including working with design control and requirements in a regulated environment, or comparable experience from another highly regulated industry.

• Experience in cross-functional product development involving hardware, electronics, mechanics, and software, ideally within medical devices or a related engineering or consultancy environment.

• A strong systems engineering mindset combined with a practical approach to developing robust and reliable product solutions.

• The ability to work independently, take ownership, and remain pragmatic and solution-oriented while actively sharing knowledge and collaborating within a global team.

• Experience working with an OEM, contract manufacturer, or external development partner would be an advantage.

• A solid understanding of relevant standards for medical electrical equipment, such as IEC 60601-1, IEC 60601-2-18, and ISO 80601-2-18, and experience translating regulatory and standards requirements into practical product development activities would also be an advantage

As Ambu is a global company, it is important that you communicate fluently in English. Only applications submitted in English will be considered.

**How To Apply

**We invite candidates for interviews on a continuous basis, so please do not hesitate to apply via our career site at ambu.com.

Your application will be treated confidentially.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in plant-microbe interactions
jobs.description:
Postdoc in plant-microbe interactions at AU Flakkebjerg Aarhus University
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, is offering a postdoctoral position in plant-biofertilizer interactions, starting 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. The position will be available for a 24-month period.

You will be part of a research environment focusing on plant-microbe interactions. You will be contributing to specifically the area of how different cereal genotypes interact with soil microbiomes and biofertilizers, and the focus of your position will be to study i) root colonization efficiency of biologicals on a range of cereal lines and ii) the effect of cereal cultivar mixtures on root microbiomes.

We expect that you will be an important part of the research environment and that you will contribute positively to the social working environment. We also expect that you will take part in our teaching activities and that you will report research results in high-impact scientific journals.

Your profile
We are searching for a highly motivated candidate who has:

• A PhD in plant-microbe interactions or similar
• Collaborative skills and ability to demonstrate commitment in teams. A fondness of taking the initiative and the motivation to pursue a scientific career
• Documented experience in scientific writing and publication in peer-reviewed scientific journals
• Research experience in areas of microbial ecology and plant biology
Additional qualifications
Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

• Teaching and supervision experience at the BSc and MSc level
• Interest and experience in developing competitive national and international research applications
• Experience in planning and conducting laboratory work within plants, microbiology and greenhouse experiments
• Insight into plant physiology and nutrition
• Experience with high-throughput sequencing (metabarcoding and RNASeq) and advanced microscopy
Who we are
At the Department of Agroecology, our main goal is to contribute to sustainable solutions to some of the world’s biggest problems within the areas of soil, plants, animals, humans, and the environment. We want to make a difference by contributing to both fundamental knowledge generation and the attainment of sustainable production systems via innovative research, contracted policy advice, and education. We offer professional laboratories, greenhouses, semi-field, and field-scale research facilities, advanced computing capacities as well as an extensive national and international researcher network. The department consists of nine research sections with around 350 highly skilled employees, of which approximately 50% are scientific staff. More information can be found here.

We believe in encouraging inclusion, acceptance, and understanding by employing staff who bring unique perspectives to our department.

What we offer
• A collaborative, international research environment that combines high academic standards with an informal and supportive atmosphere. We value accountability, curiosity, flexibility, and teamwork in everything we do.
• An inclusive and respectful workplace culture, where mutual trust, kindness, and professional dialogue are part of daily life. We encourage open communication and develop a cohesive sense of community across teams and disciplines.
• A flexible working environment that supports work-life balance and individual needs.
• An active institutional commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion – in recruitment, career development, and everyday interactions.
• An innovative and meaningful workplace where your work contributes to solving real-world challenges. No two days are alike, and we welcome creative thinking and new ideas.
• Support for international researchers and their families, including Relocation Service and an Expat Partner Programme
Living and working in Denmark
• Subsidised childcare and free education from primary school through university.
• Universal healthcare for you and your family as residents.
• Five weeks of paid holiday per year.
• Generous parental leave – up to 52 weeks shared between parents, with full or partial salary.
Place of Work
The place of work is Aarhus University, Campus Flakkebjerg. The affiliation will be with the Department of Agroecology.

Contact information 
For further information about the position, please contact Mogens Nicolaisen at mn@agro.au.dk.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

About Aarhus University

Aarhus University is an academically diverse and research-intensive university with a strong commitment to high-quality research and education and the development of society nationally and globally. The university offers an inspiring research and teaching environment for its 37,500 students, including PhD students, and has 9,000 employees (full-time equivalents) and an annual revenue of EUR 1.2 billion. Learn more at international.au.dk

jobs.occupation: PhD Fellowships in Quantum Science and Technology - QISTgrad Individual PhD Projects
jobs.description:
Shape the Future of Quantum Science
Are you curious about quantum science and eager to develop your own research ideas? Would you like to work with leading researchers while becoming part of a vibrant and supportive interdisciplinary research community?

The Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Copenhagen (UCPH) invite applications for fully funded PhD fellowships within the VILLUM Quantum Science and Technology Graduate Program (QISTgrad). The programme brings together researchers and students from a broad range of disciplines to advance quantum science and technology and train the next generation of quantum researchers.

We welcome applicants from diverse academic backgrounds and encourage applications from candidates who are excited about exploring how their knowledge and perspectives can contribute to quantum research.

The expected start date is 1 September 2027 or according to mutual agreement.

Design Your Own Research Direction
Unlike many PhD positions, QISTgrad offers a unique opportunity to shape your own research project. Successful applicants will develop their research project in collaboration with a supervisor (or supervisors) at either DTU or UCPH. You do not need to identify a supervisor before applying. Instead, successful candidates will receive support in finding the most suitable supervisors and mentors across DTU and UCPH.

From 2026 to 2030, DTU and UCPH will jointly offer a total of 24 fully funded PhD fellowships. We are currently offering at least 4 positions with an expected start on 1 September 2027. Next call is anticipated in November 2028.

Who are we looking for?
We are looking for applicants who are curious, motivated, creative, and eager to develop as researchers. You may come from a variety of academic backgrounds and do not need previous experience in quantum science. What matters most is your ability to think critically, explore new ideas, and demonstrate how your academic background can contribute to quantum research.

If you have a Bachelor qualification or have not completed a master’s program equivalent to a Danish 2-year (120 ECTS) master’s degree, you might like to enroll in a combined program with a Master of Science (MSc) in Quantum Information Science - Study Programmes on University of Copenhagen followed by a PhD.

Why Join QISTgrad?
A fully funded PhD fellowship; Freedom to help define your own research project; Access to world-class research environments at DTU and UCPH; Interdisciplinary collaboration; Academic and career mentoring; Networking events and workshops; International collaborations; A supportive and inclusive research community.

Application Requirements
The primary objective of the application process is to evaluate your research potential, creativity, and motivation. Instead of focusing primarily on prior quantum research experience, applicants complete a questionnaire that demonstrates interests, ideas, experience, and readiness for PhD education. Fill in the Questionnaire: Apply for fellowship – University of Copenhagen and add this to your application.

Selection Process
The application process will follow three phases (see Calls for fellowship – University of Copenhagen). All applications will be reviewed in phase one, and selected applicants will be shortlisted for assessment in phase two. In phase three, a number of qualified candidates will be invited for an interview successful applicants will then be assisted in finding supervisors and mentors, in consultation with the Selection Committee of the program, and be enrolled in the appropriate PhD-school at either UCPH or DTU: VILLUM Quantum Science and Technology Graduate Program – University of Copenhagen. Both universities are located in greater area of Copenhagen, Denmark and you will be expected to relocate to Copenhagen.

The PhD programme 
Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either: 

• Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree. 
• Option B (only possible at UCPH): An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.
Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme

Qualifications needed for the regular programme
To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to research in quantum science and technology. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countriesand Assessment database.

Terms of employment in the regular programme 
Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years. 

Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at DTU or UCPH. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant. 

Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure. 

You will be employed either by DTU or UPCH. 

Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme (Only a possibility at UCPH)

Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 
If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database. 

Terms of the integrated programme
To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Quantum research (QIS) or related MSc programmes, such as Physics or Nanoscience. 

Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see: For UCPH www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax. 

When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme 
(ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme at UCPH)
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project
We are looking for the following qualifications:

• Professional qualifications relevant to the PhD project
• Relevant publications
• Relevant work experience
• Other relevant professional activities
• Curious mind-set with a strong interest in quantum research
• Good language skills
Application and Assessment Procedure
Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

Please include: 

• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 
• A filled in questionnaire (Apply for fellowship – University of Copenhagen )
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position (max. four pages)
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 
• Publication list (if possible) with links to articles (do not include full articles)
• Do not include your full master’s thesis
Application deadline: 
The deadline for applications is 18 January 2027, 23:59 GMT +1. 

We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

The further process 
After the deadline, a Selection Committee consisting of Researchers from both DTU and UCPH will assess the qualifications and experience and create a shortlist of applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. 

Interviews with selected candidates are expected to be held during spring of 2027. The timeframe of the process is described here: Apply for fellowship – University of Copenhagen.

Please note that by applying for the QISTgrad Ph.D.-fellowship you grant UCPH and DTU the right to exchange your personal data. 

Questions
For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact qistgrad@science.ku.dk. 

General information about PhD study at the UCPH is available at the PhD School’s website: https://science.ku.dk/phd/.

General information about PhD study at the DTU is available at Get a PhD education at DTU.

The University of Copenhagen and Technical University of Denmark wish to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark
jobs.description:
Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark

Your impact begins here

As Senior Director, Injectables Quality Denmark, you will lead Quality across four Danish sites and rethink how Quality works alongside manufacturing. You will bring leaders together, challenge established ways of working and drive simplification, productivity and innovation through technology, AI and new operating models. All while ensuring patient safety, compliance and reliable supply. Your impact will show in stronger collaboration across Hillerød, Gentofte, Bagsværd and Kalundborg, and in building a high-performing Quality organisation where colleagues feel empowered to challenge, improve and drive change.

What you’ll bring

You are a senior leader with pharmaceutical industry experience, who has led change in complex environments, who earns trust across sites and functions, and who has brought people with you through periods of transformation.

• Substantial experience from the pharmaceutical industry, with a strong background in quality (QA or QC), in manufacturing, or a combination of both, and strong GMP expertise.

• Proven experience as a leader of leader, preferably across more than one site, with responsibility for talent development, succession planning, budgets and organisational performance.

• A strong track record of driving transformation and operational improvements, including productivity gains, inspections and Quality support for new products or expansions.

• Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders across functions and countries, including digitalisation, automation or changes to operating models.

• Leadership that builds trust and psychological safety, and the courage to set a clear direction when change is challenging.

• Sound judgement in critical Quality decisions, balancing compliance and business needs without compromising patient safety.

What you’ll do

You will lead the Danish Injectables Quality organisation through a period of transformation, with the ambition of making Quality a stronger enabler of manufacturing performance and a competitive advantage for Novo. Lead Quality across four sites, ensuring robust GMP compliance, inspection readiness and effective quality risk management.

• Challenge existing processes, remove complexity and use technology, AI and smarter ways of working to deliver measurable productivity improvements, rather than adding headcount whenever volumes rise.

• Build one leadership team across the sites. Coach, challenge and develop leaders, set clear accountability and strengthen succession and talent pipelines.

• Help colleagues see ongoing change as progress. Set a clear direction and keep teams healthy and engaged while the way of working evolves.

• Strengthen collaboration and leverage capabilities across sites, and help shape shared set-ups across sites.

• Ensure Quality readiness for new products, capacity expansions and production ramp-up, and act as a trusted partner to manufacturing leadership.

• Take an active seat in the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, helping shape priorities across the wider Quality organisation as well as your own area.

Who you’ll work with

You will report to the VP, Drug Product Manufacturing Quality and be part of the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, contributing to the strategic direction and transformation of Quality across our international drug product manufacturing network.

You will lead an experienced leadership team responsible for an organisation of more than 240 colleagues, including specialists and Qualified Persons. You will support the Qualified Persons while respecting their independent responsibility for batch certification and release.

Your closest partners will be site and manufacturing leaders across Hillerød, Gentofte, Bagsværd and Kalundborg, alongside MSAT, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, Digital and IT, P&O and Finance. You will also work with health authorities, inspectors, auditors, suppliers and technology partners. You will be expected to put collective success ahead of local optimisation and to speak up early when things stall.

What you can expect here

You will have real scope to shape how Quality works at Novo. You will be trusted to make decisions, challenge the status quo and take ownership, with clear expectations for performance and honest feedback in both directions.

You will grow through a broad leadership remit across four sites, close collaboration with the Drug Product Manufacturing Quality leadership team, as well as the Drug Product Manufacturing Denmark Injectables leadership team and the chance to influence priorities beyond your own area. You will work at the forefront of digitalisation, automation and AI in Quality, with a team that values curiosity and decisive action.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead Quality through change, bring four sites closer together and show how Quality can make manufacturing faster and simpler, apply for the role by December 6.

For further information, please contact Executive Search Advisor, Kristoffer Baadsgaard on +45 30 77 56 05

jobs.occupation: Health & Safety Partner
jobs.description:
Health & Safety Partner

Your impact begins here

As a Health & Safety Partner, you will help our production sites turn health and safety requirements into practical action. Working across our global Drug Production Manufacturing (DPM) network, you will partner with assigned sites to strengthen compliance, prepare for audits and inspections, and continuously improve health and safety performance.

You will combine strong stakeholder management with a structured, analytical approach, helping sites understand priorities, close gaps and determine the right next steps. This is an opportunity to make a tangible impact on health and safety across an international manufacturing organisation.

What you'll bring

You know that successful health and safety work is as much about people and trust as it is about systems and requirements. You can work independently, challenge constructively and turn complex information into practical solutions.

We are looking for someone who:

• Has 3–5 years of experience as a Health & Safety Partner or in a similar role.

• Has strong stakeholder-management skills and can build trust and productive relationships across functions, cultures and geographies.

• Works in a structured and independent way, with a solution-oriented mindset and the ability to think ahead.

• Has strong analytical and critical-thinking skills and is comfortable using health and safety data to identify gaps, trends and appropriate next steps.

• Has experience with audits, health and safety management systems or similar compliance activities. Experience from a highly regulated industry is an advantage.

• Brings project management experience and skills, as we aim to include our coming employee in development tasks across the department.

• Is fluent in written and spoken English. Danish is an advantage, but not a requirement.

Experience with ISO 45001 and health and safety IT systems will be useful in supporting the responsibilities of the role.

What you'll do

As Health & Safety Partner, you will be allocated to production sites and serve as a key link between the sites, DPM and Novo Nordisk Corporate Health & Safety. Your responsibilities will include:

• Partnering with assigned production sites to implement Novo Nordisk health and safety requirements and translate strategic priorities into practical actions.

• Supporting sites before, during and after audits and inspections, including gap analyses, preparation and management of findings, and helping sites maintain a strong state of audit readiness.

• Coordinating and supporting preparation for ISO 45001 recertification and contributing to Health and Safety Management Reviews across DPM.

• Using health and safety data, indicators, KPIs and reporting flows to identify trends, challenge assumptions and guide decisions and priorities.

• Supporting initiatives related to areas such as Life Safety Rules, ergonomics, safety culture, emergency preparedness and health and safety targets.

• Working closely with site Health & Safety Partners and other stakeholders to clarify priorities, coordinate deliverables and identify logical, solution-focused next steps.

Success in the role requires you to balance independent ownership with close collaboration. You will be accountable for supporting your allocated sites in progressing their health and safety agenda, including successful preparation for audits.

Who you'll work with

You will join DPM Security, Health & Safety, a central department anchored in Production Support Operational Excellence. The team supports the business in meeting Novo Nordisk Corporate Health & Safety and Global Security requirements and connects corporate functions with production sites by translating requirements into practical direction and solutions.

Your stakeholders will include Health & Safety Partners at production sites, colleagues across DPM, other project and functional stakeholders, and Corporate Health & Safety. Because DPM operates a global network of factories across Asia, Europe, North America and South America, the role includes approximately 15–20% travel.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to work with health and safety at both site and network level, giving you broad exposure to an international manufacturing organisation. The role combines hands-on partnership with data analysis, compliance activities and cross-functional collaboration, while giving you significant ownership of your allocated sites.

For this position, the annual base salary ranges between DKK 651,000 and DKK 956,900, depending on the position level. Placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s competencies, qualifications, knowledge, and relevant experience.

The compensation package may include short-term and/or long-term incentive schemes as well as additional employee benefits, depending on job level, geographical location, professional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Start now

If you want to use your Health & Safety expertise to build trusted partnerships and help production sites translate requirements, audit findings and data into meaningful improvements, this could be your next opportunity.

We would like the successful candidate to start as soon as possible.

Application deadline: 26/11

Location: Lyngby

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis.

jobs.occupation: Tenure-track Assistant or Associate Professor Functional Biology and Ecology of Marine Animals
jobs.description:
Department of Biology, Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen, Denmark

  The Department of Biology at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a position as Tenure-track or Associate Professor in functional biology and ecology of marine animals. The position is set to be filled by June 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, pending negotiation.

  Position Overview
 We are looking for a passionate, innovative and collaborative researcher with expertise in hypothesis driven research on the functional biology and experimental ecology of marine animals. The ideal candidate will complement and strengthen our existing research areas, and take advantage of our experimental facilities and easy access to different coastal ecosystems. We expect the successful candidate to take a leading role in establishing an externally funded research program and take an active part in developing existing and new courses in the teaching curriculum of the section.

  Key responsibilities include:

   	
• Leading research initiatives and securing third-party funding 	
• Teaching and supervising students at undergraduate, graduate, and PhD levels, with primary teaching responsibilities in the biology degree program 	
• Disseminating research and scientific results to the public 	
• Participating in departmental committees and other tasks as requested   The Research Environment
 The candidate will join the Section for Marine Biology, which operates across both the Copenhagen and Helsingør campuses. The position will be based in Helsingør, where laboratory and office facilities will be provided. The section’s research encompasses a wide range of topics within marine biology including aquatic microbiology and virology, sensory biology, physiology and functional biology of marine organisms, climate change biology, aquaculture, coral reef biology, deep sea biology and the diversity, phylogeny, and evolution of metazoans and protists. Studies are conducted across polar, temperate, and (sub)tropical ecosystems.

  The section boasts modern laboratories equipped with state-of-the-art tools and infrastructure for experimental research including sea-water facilities for animal keeping. This also includes specialized labs for microenvironmental analyses, respirometry, electrophysiology, advanced bioimaging, and DNA and RNA analyses. Additionally, our research vessel, Ophelia, and the proximity to diverse marine habitats in Øresund and other areas provide an excellent platform for a broad range of biological studies.

  We encourage interdisciplinary collaborations within the department and externally with industry and public research institutions, where synergistic benefits are evident.

  Qualifications and Profile
 Applicants should have a strong background in functional biology and experimental ecology of marine animals and their response to environmental changes. Applicants must demonstrate a proven ability to conduct independent, original, and hypothesis-driven experimental research at an international level. 

  Applicants should be capable of teaching a variety of topics within animal science and ecology in the BSc and MSc biology programs and are expected to contribute by developing new courses.

  Qualifications for Tenure-track Assistant Professor level: 

   	
• A strong publication trajectory in high-level, international, peer-reviewed ISI journals 	
• Experience with personal research grants or participation (by name) in major grants 	
• Research plans and publication records that demonstrate clear potential for attracting external funding 	
• Academic standing reflecting internationally competitive research and/or high potential to make a future scientific impact at the international level 	
• Documented university-level teaching experience is advantageous but not mandatory 	
• If not already holding formal pedagogical qualifications, the candidate must complete pedagogical training equivalent to the University of Copenhagen’s Teaching and Learning in Higher Education Program for Assistant Professors   Qualifications for Associate Professor level: 

   	
• A substantial publication record in high-level, international, peer-reviewed ISI journals 	
• A proven track record of securing major external research funding 	
• Documented university-level experience in delivering high-quality undergraduate/graduate teaching, with the ability to explain and reflect on own teaching practices 	
• Formal pedagogical training or supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen’s teacher training program 	
• Managerial and outreach experience   The Department of Biology (BIO) employs around 425 academic and technical staff and hosts research programs and teaching curricula that cover all major biological sub-disciplines. University rankings typically place the field of biology and biochemistry at the University of Copenhagen first in Denmark and among the top 15-25 universities globally. We offer PhD, BSc, and MSc programs in biology, biochemistry, molecular biomedicine, and bioinformatics, engaging around 1,800 students.

  The department is committed to equality of opportunity and to creating an inclusive working environment that reflects the diversity of society. At BIO, we see diversity as a strength. We highly value a safe and collaborative working atmosphere, and offer a friendly and thriving international research environment with opportunities to build internationally competitive research groups. Excellent opportunities are available for research funding to establish oneself in Denmark.

  Learn out more about working at BIO here.

  Copenhagen is among the 10 most livable cities in the world with a vibrant music, dance and theater culture, world class restaurants, an extensive public transportation system and excellent opportunities for biking in the city. Life for families is made easy by a publicly supported daycare and healthcare system, dual career opportunities, maternity/paternity leave and six weeks of annual vacation.

  Assessment of applicants 
 Assessment of applicants for the tenure-track assistant professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, internationally competitive research. The ability to attract external funding will be considered together with outreach qualifications. Teaching qualifications are not mandatory but documented teaching qualifications and teaching experience will be considered.

  Assessment of applicants for the associate professorship will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  University of Copenhagen’s criteria for recognising merit
 General criteria apply to the appointment of assistant professor / associate professor at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, Innovation & societal impact, organizational contribution and leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement.

  Please read more here:
 
 For tenure-track assistant professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5a_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Assistant_professors.pdf

  For associate professors: https://jobportal.ku.dk/videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-videnskabelige-stillinger/kriterier-for-meritering-maj-2026/5b_Criteria_for_recognising_merit_-Associate_professors.pdf

  Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here

  The Appointment Committee will prepare a short-list of applicants at both levels to be assessed by an Assessment Committee. Note that being on the short-list, is not equivalent to being assessed qualified for the position. Short-listed candidate may potentially be deemed “not qualified” by the Assessment Committee. 

  A sub-set of the qualified short-listed candidates will be selected for a formal interview by the Appointment Committee.  Invited candidates may also be given the opportunity to visit the department to meet with the faculty and the Head of Department, and to give a research presentation.

  Terms of employment
 The position is open from June 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Employment is either as tenure-track assistant professor or associate professor under the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  We encourage women and members of other underrepresented groups to apply, as we are committed to diversifying our department and fostering an inclusive environment.

  Information on tenure-track program
 An assigned mentor will provide the tenure-track assistant professor with guidance related to career development, other academic topics, and administrative procedures.

  Performance of the tenure-track assistant professor will be followed via internal yearly evaluations and a mid-term and final international evaluation by an assessment committee. If the ‘final appraisal’ is positive you will be promoted to associate professor. Performance and progression towards the criteria above will be evaluated with due consideration of differences between research fields.

  Further information
 For more information about the Department of Biology and the various research sections, please visit our website https://www1.bio.ku.dk/english/.

  Inquiries about the position can be made to Head of Department, Professor Edda Klipp (edda.klipp@bio.ku.dk) or Head of Section, Associate Professor Anders Garm (algarm@bio.ku.dk). 

  International candidates may find information on living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. Useful information is also available at The International Staff Mobility office (ISM) at the University of Copenhagen (https://ism.ku.dk). ISM offers a variety of services to international researchers coming to and working at the University of Copenhagen.

  Filing of application
 The position may be applied for at the tenure-track assistant professor and Associate Professor level. Please note that it is possible to apply at more than one level. If applied at more than one level, separate applications must be submitted (see below).

  The application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Applying for the tenure-track assistant professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including: 	 		
• Please describe and document international network and relations 		
• Please describe and document internationally based activities 		
• Positions held at universities/research institutions outside Denmark 		
• Outreach activities, i.e. popular lectures or other activities in the media 		
• Grants held, personal or in part. Career development grants. 		
• [Other qualifications can be filled in by Department] 	 	 	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent) 	
• Research plan - description of current and future research plans 	
• If available, description and documentation of teaching and supervision experience and qualifications- please describe and document: 	 		
• Experience with supervision of BSc and MSc students 		
• Teaching experience 		
• Formal pedagogical training 	 	 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of up to 5 particularly relevant papers   Applying for the associate professorship please include 

   	
• Curriculum vitae including information about external funding  	
• Diplomas (Master and PhD degree or equivalent)  	
• Research plan – description of current and future research plans  	
• Description and documentation of teaching experience and qualifications according to university guidelines 	
• Complete publication list 	
• Separate reprints of 5 particularly relevant papers   Deadline for applications is 20 December 2026 at 23:59 GMT+2

  After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Interview Committee.

  Interviews will be held on 8 April 2027. Invited candidates may also be invited to visit the Department of Biology, to meet with the faculty and the Head of Department, and to give a research presentation. 

  Please refer to the following numbers in future communication in this case: 

  Tenure-track Assistant Professor in Functional Biology and Ecology of Marine Animals 211-0265/26-2N

  Associate Professor in Functional Biology and Ecology of Marine Animals 211-0769/26-2E

  We very much look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Sufficiency-based Building Design and Energy System Optimisation
jobs.description:
Are you interested in understanding how the concept of sufficiency affects the optimal design of buildings and their energy systems, and can you contribute to the development of the CEBE programme? Then the Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering invites you to apply for a 2-year postdoc position.

Expected start date and duration of employment
This is a 2–year position from 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible. This is a fixed-term position to end on 28 February 2029.

Job description
We are offering a Postdoctoral research position in Building Design and Energy System Optimisation, with particular focus on:

• Optimization-oriented modelling of buildings and their energy system.
• Formulation of optimization frameworks, and integration of multidisciplinary aspects.
• Cross-domain collaboration with social science, on the concept of sufficiency in buildings.
This position is part of the larger CEBE research program, within Research Field 6 - Sufficiency, well-being and energy efficiency. The research tasks will be carried out in a collaborative setting, at Aarhus University with Michael Dahl Knudsen, and with continuous cooperation with RF6 researchers from AAU, DTU, and SDU.

Your profile
The ideal candidate has:

• A PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Energy Engineering, Civil Engineering, or similar.
• Strong background in one or more of the following areas: Building physics, occupant behaviour modelling, energy systems modelling, numerical optimization methods.
• Documented experience in handling research challenges
• Solid programming skills (e.g. Python, Matlab)
• Interest in interdisciplinary work involving social science
• Strong written and verbal English communication skills
Who we are
The Department of Civil and Architectural Engineering at Aarhus University is a growing engineering environment with a clear vision for the future of the built environment.

Established in 2021, the department today includes more than 100 researchers and educators and around 1.050 students.

We conduct research and education within structural engineering, geotechnics, architectural engineering and design, sustainability, construction management, climate adaptation, indoor climate, building materials, and digital technologies.

The construction sector is facing major challenges related to climate, resource consumption, and the way we design and build our cities and buildings.

Through research, education, and collaboration with industry and public sector partners, we contribute to developing technological solutions that support a more sustainable built environment.

Our research and development activities are closely connected to the needs of industry and society, and many projects are carried out in collaboration with companies, public authorities, and other research environments. This ensures that the knowledge and technologies developed at the department are relevant in practice and create value beyond the university.

Education is a central part of the department’s identity. We offer Bachelor’s, Master’s, and PhD programmes in engineering and continuously work to improve the connection between research, teaching, and practice.

Across our programmes, students work with real-world challenges, current technologies, and sustainable solutions for the construction sector.

What we offer
We offer an innovative and collaborative teaching and research environment with close interaction between students, researchers, and industry partners.

The department provides well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories, and access to shared technical facilities.

We offer an interdisciplinary environment with national, international, and industrial collaborators.

Our academic environment is built on collaboration, knowledge sharing, and professional dialogue.

The workplace is characterised by professionalism, flexibility, and a healthy work–life balance.

The department is located at Navitas on the waterfront in Aarhus, Denmark

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is Inge Lehmanns Gade 10, Navitas, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Contact information
For further information, please contact: Associate Professor, Massimo Fiorentini, +45 9352 2961, massimo@cae.au.dk

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 14 December 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The overwhelming majority of coffee and cocoa are produced in the tropics, and represent vast economic drivers globally as these products continue to transform from commodities to luxury goods. Alongside other factors, the quality of these goods is largely influenced by post-harvest processing, which modulates microbial activity, in turn leading to differences in sensory impact. Complex microbial dynamics affect fermentation outcomes and sensory attributes, and understanding these dynamics and how relevant microbial consortia can be mobilised to modulate these outcomes pose challenging questions that can lead to multiple applications, including ones with health implications. This project aims to unravel some of the underlying microbial dynamics of tropical fermentations such as coffee, cocoa, or other traditional tropical fermentation, utilizing a combination of metagenomics, strain characterization, and solid-state fermentation.

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. The job

• Analyse metagenomic profiles of artisanal tropical fermentations
• Characterise extant yeast and bacteria for relevant traits for fermentative capability and other functional capacities
• Perform solid state fermentations in controlled settings to achieve targeted outcomes
• Evaluate fermentations via microbiology, molecular biology, and analytic chemistry

Are you curious about the diverse microbial interactions in fermentation, whilst eager to contribute towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in microbial consortia for solid-state fermentation! 

Existing microbial food productions have largely focused on liquid state fermentation as the main production strategy under industrial settings. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Demand Estimation for Large-Scale Transport Networks using Travel Surveys and 5G Data - DTU Management
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about data analytics, optimization, transport, and environment? Do you want to work on a research project that has a concrete impact on society? 

We invite you to apply for a full-time PhD position at DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) as part of an international Alliance PhD collaboration between DTU Management and Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IPP), France. The project “ASTRA” (Analytics for Spatio-Temporal Regional trAnsport models) explores how emerging data sources can be better integrated into demand estimation, and aims to develop a working prototype for the national Danish transport model.

Knowing how many people travel, where and when is the foundation of every transport model, and ultimately of decisions on infrastructure investments, transport policy and the green transition. Yet estimating mobility demand for large networks remains one of the main bottlenecks in transport modelling. The problem is highly non-linear, underdetermined and difficult to solve for large-scale networks, and existing methods often rely on proprietary, non-reproducible data and an oversimplified representation of travel behaviour. As a result, they often fail to represent travel decisions realistically, which can lead to misallocated infrastructure and ineffective policy interventions. At the same time, new data sources are emerging. Mobile networks, and in particular 5G antennas, continuously capture anonymous mobility traces, while travel surveys provide rich behavioural and socio-economic information, but only for small samples, and are rarely used in demand estimation.

The ASTRA project will develop a demand estimation framework that combines high-resolution behavioural data, such as the Danish National Travel Survey, with large-scale, low-resolution data, such as traffic counts and mobile phone network data. The aim is to realistically capture behaviour while remaining applicable to national-scale networks. A key expected outcome of the project is a demand estimation model for the Danish national transport model, the Green Mobility Model (GMM). Collaboration with the Danish Road Directorate (Vejdirektoratet) is therefore anticipated, to ensure real-life deployment.

Transportation Systems Modelling section
Transport systems are a vital part of society and the economy, enabling movement of people and goods and making it imperative to plan and operate them in an efficient, equitable and sustainable manner. However, transport systems are complex, involving heterogeneous travellers who make choices in multimodal networks that are dynamic and prone to congestion. Therefore, gaining a fundamental understanding of transport systems and developing methodologies that can model them realistically are critical.

Towards this end, the Transportation Systems Modelling Section focusses on (i) developing methodologies that ensure behavioural realism, theoretical consistency and tractability in large real-world transport networks, (ii) gaining behavioural insights by utilising rich data sources, and (iii) designing and optimising transport systems, including road pricing schemes, bicycle networks and public transport systems. We have a combined focus across modes of transport, including bicycle, car and public transport.
